newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says would keep SERPS state pension.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says would keep SERPS state pension.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party would keep the state earnings-related pension scheme, which the ruling Conservative Party is expected to abolish, Labour's social security spokeswoman Harriet Harman said.
"We would keep it in its limited form to give people the choice of carrying on being in SERPS," she said in an interview with BBC Radio 4.

Keeping SERPS would mean the UK continued to have a state-based pension framework mainly for the low paid and those such as carers for the sick who are contributing to society but not actually earning money and therefore could not afford a private pension scheme, Harman said.
"But we do agree that there is a need for a good, new, second-tier funded pension," she said.
The Conservative Party is expected to announce plans today to abolish SERPS and replace it with compulsory private pensions.

Newspapers say the party believes getting rid of SERPS will allow big public spending savings in the long term and will help their campaign for re-election. A general election is widely expected to be held on May 1.
